options.error_type: confuses transcript review with grapheme-to-phoneme conversion
options.rationale: Mapping written letters to phonemes is grapheme-to-phoneme conversion in speech synthesis. It does not support reviewing recognized transcript words against audio.
options.better_fit: Use this when text-to-speech must pronounce unknown words.

feedback.intrinsic: The dashboard would focus on pronunciation instead of helping agents check questionable transcript words.
feedback.instructional: Grapheme-to-phoneme maps letters to sounds. Confidence and timestamps connect recognized words to certainty and audio timing.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Confidence scores and word-level timestamps help agents inspect uncertain transcript segments and hear the matching audio.

payload.prompt: A product manager asks why a recognizer trained only on English speech cannot handle Mandarin tones in a new voice assistant. Which points should guide the decision?

options.rationale: Phonemes are the smallest sound units that distinguish words, and they are language-specific. Training on one language's sound units does not automatically cover another language's tones.

options.text: The model needs retraining for Mandarin tones.
options.rationale: A recognizer trained on English phonemes cannot recognize Mandarin tones without retraining. Retraining is needed so the recognizer can learn the required sound patterns.

options.text: Post-processing can reliably add missing tone recognition.
options.error_type: confuses phoneme training limits with text cleanup
options.rationale: Post-processing refines decoded text after recognition. It cannot add recognition of missing language-specific tones.
options.better_fit: Use post-processing for formatting, filtering, punctuation, and similar cleanup after recognition.

feedback.intrinsic: The voice assistant could still miss Mandarin tones because cleanup cannot make up for missing sound training.
feedback.instructional: Tone recognition is learned during recognition training. Post-processing only works on text after recognition has already happened.

options.text: Timestamps teach the model new language sounds.
options.error_type: confuses timing metadata with phoneme recognition
options.rationale: Timestamps show when words occurred in audio. They do not teach new phonemes or tones.
options.better_fit: Use timestamps when a user needs to jump to a word's audio moment.

feedback.intrinsic: The team would know where words occur in audio but still lack Mandarin tone recognition.
feedback.instructional: Timing metadata helps review audio. Language-specific sound recognition requires training on those sounds.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Phonemes are language-specific, so Mandarin tones require suitable recognition training rather than cleanup or timing metadata.
